points: Before a page can load, a browser opens a TCP connection, sets up encryption with TLS, and only then sends an HTTP request, and each step waits for a full round trip.
Distance sets the cost, not bandwidth, so the fixes all spend fewer round trips: reuse open connections, use TLS 1.3, resume old sessions, or move to QUIC.
Google and Meta moved real traffic to QUIC and HTTP/3 and measured faster searches, fewer errors and fewer video stalls, at the price of more server CPU.
Cloudflare found HTTP/3 faster to the first byte but slightly behind HTTP/2 on larger pages, and warns that 0-RTT data can be replayed.
